name: Alexei Navalny
role: Russian opposition leader and anti-corruption campaigner (1976-2024)
summary: Navalny led the Anti-Corruption Foundation and ran for Moscow mayor in 2013 and, unregistered, for president in 2018. His programme combined a compact, deregulated economy with higher minimum wages and healthcare spending, a parliamentary or presidential-parliamentary republic with term limits and federalism, an all-volunteer army and lustration. He mixed anti-immigration politics (a visa regime with Central Asia) with strong opposition to imperial expansion, and from 2022 demanded Russian withdrawal to Ukraine's 1991 borders.

abortion-legal.rationale: He described himself as quite liberal on abortion.

conscription.rationale: He repeatedly called the draft inefficient and unjust, 'a tax on the poor', and committed to abolish it for an all-volunteer army.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He argued that power must rest on honest elections, alternation of power and people's rule, and described Putin as having usurped it.

constituent-assembly.rationale: He listed free general elections and convening a Constitutional Assembly as the way to dismantle the regime.

decide-locally.rationale: His platform moves tax revenue and powers to regions and municipalities and says the reform should transfer as much authority as possible to the city level.

democracy-best.rationale: He said that had the Communist candidate won in 1996 the pendulum would have swung back through normal competition, and he stressed that opponents of democracy do not trust voters.

direct-votes.rationale: His programme extends the rights of the Duma and regional assemblies to hold referendums and citizen polls, which it calls direct democracy.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He said Russia should take part in a joint security system with NATO members.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He called for a justice system that makes Russian citizens equal before the law.

free-trade.rationale: His foreign-economic programme sets a free-trade zone between the EU and the Eurasian union as the ultimate goal and seeks to remove barriers to Russian exports.

legalize-drugs.rationale: He called legalisation of marijuana impossible at this stage and said drugs are evil, while demanding decriminalisation of small personal quantities and treatment.

limit-guns.rationale: He said he is at the far liberal end on distribution of weapons and co-signed the NAROD call to legalise short-barreled firearms for self-defence.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He calls Russia's state-dominated economy a twisted capitalism that hinders growth and proposes demonopolisation, deregulation and a compact state.

military-superiority.rationale: He said Russia's glory does not rest on territory or military power and promised to cut the military and police budget.

night-watchman-state.rationale: He wants the state to provide healthcare, education, pensions and transport, which goes beyond protection from violence.

one-party-rule.rationale: He stated that Russia should be a parliamentary republic based on alternation of power through fair elections and demanded access to elections for parties.

open-borders.rationale: He proposed a visa regime with Central Asia and Transcaucasia and objected that any Uzbek citizen can enter Russia freely.

party-controls-media.rationale: He said fighting corruption is impossible while media are not free and that government must prevent censorship and monopolised access to information.

people-in-arms.rationale: He holds that a professional army is the main factor of Russia's security and proposed an all-volunteer military.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: He wrote that officials must serve society, the state and the law, not a specific boss.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He described the ruling elite as bribetakers who use office for enrichment, and said no 'system liberal' he knew did anything useful in office.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: He said in an interview that Russia should aim to join the European Union.

private-courts-defense.rationale: His judicial reform rebuilds independent state courts, with elected justices of the peace and public recordings, and does not privatise them.

property-fundamental.rationale: He pledged courts that protect private property from illegal takeovers, but also proposed a compensational tax on owners of 1990s privatisations.

public-ownership.rationale: His platform abolishes state corporations, sells non-core assets and says large state monopolies should not exist.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: He proposed raising the minimum wage to 25 thousand rubles so that tens of millions escape poverty, within a few years.

reduce-immigration.rationale: He backs a visa regime and legal entry, calling illegal immigration a top issue, but says migration is not bad and Russia needs labour through quotas.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He called for a real decrease of business regulation and of inspectors' powers, while creating a competition commission against monopolies.

rehabilitation.rationale: His programme makes a restorative approach to disrupted social relations the main principle of justice and calls for humanising criminal law and prisons.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: He proposed a lustration law and commission to investigate political repressions and name those responsible, and a chamber to lustrate judges.

separated-powers.rationale: He called the division of competences and separation of powers essential to prevent over-concentration of power and proposed checks and balances.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He would stop subsidising inefficient state companies and 'priority projects' and says economic projects must be funded by investors, not taxpayers.

state-harmful.rationale: He wants a compact state that still provides medicine, education, transport and pensions, and a strong judiciary and police.

strong-leader.rationale: He wrote that the model for Russia is not strong power and a firm hand, and argued for a parliamentary republic to cut one person's power.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: His programme aims at a free-trade zone between the EU and the Eurasian union and recognising EU and US certificates, not shielding domestic industry.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He called imperialism and the urge to seize territory the most harmful and destructive path and said Russia is big enough.

total-state.rationale: He wants a compact state that does not intervene in economic life, with security officials' powers reduced.

universal-healthcare.rationale: His platform makes the state provider of medicine as a core service and promises to double healthcare spending.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: He proposed limiting the president to two terms of four years, whether consecutive or not.

notes: Positions are taken from his own platform, op-eds and interviews (2011-2023); he never held office, so there is no record of acts and campaign programme answers are medium at most. Themes searched: economy, government, society, world, liberty, means, technology and ecology; nothing found in his own words on same-sex marriage, the death penalty, nuclear power, climate or religion in public life (a 2014 blog post only reports polls, and a 2013 Reuters item on gay rallies was cut off by a paywall), so those stay null. His 2014-2015 line on Crimea (a fair referendum) changed in 2023 to demanding Ukraine's 1991 borders; no statement here depends on it. Local corpora searched: MediaSum (only interpreted snippets without usable positions).
